selection.name: Dagu (C03)
selection.role: Provisional local workflow engine: direct shell/YAML authoring, schedules, retries, visible history and authenticated MCP. Linux x86_64 and macOS arm64 binaries are available.

basis.shows: Documents local script workflows, scheduling, retries, history/UI, CLI and authenticated MCP without an external database.
Released 2026-09-29, including Linux amd64 and Darwin arm64 assets.
Default-branch commit dated 2026-10-02 UTC; repository is unarchived and has recent issue activity.
Ubuntu unit shard succeeded at the v2.18.1 release commit; its sampled check rollup was SUCCESS.
Tests explicitly permit execution to continue when native resource enforcement fails. Linux CPU/memory cgroups therefore require verification; they do not establish a mandatory PID bound.
Tests workflow cancellation and pending-retry cancellation by run ID, without proving detached-descendant cleanup.
Stale-run repair marks interrupted active work failed; this establishes status repair rather than crash-safe external-effect replay.

selection.name: systemd (C05)
selection.role: Complementary Linux supervisor. Configure per-workflow units with explicit PID, memory and time limits; use systemd-run/systemctl for agent integration and cgroup-scoped cancellation.
selection.install_command: sudo apt-get update -y && sudo apt-get install systemd systemd-sysv -y

basis.shows: Default KillMode=control-group stops remaining unit processes, with TERM followed by configured timeout and KILL escalation.
Documents TasksMax and MemoryMax through cgroup PID and memory controls; limits must be configured explicitly.
Relevant upstream tests cover nested/disowned processes and stopping a cgroup after its original parent exits.
Ubuntu noble CI succeeded at the examined default-branch commit.
The same commit's Fedora sanitizer job failed; the overall rollup was FAILURE. Failure cause was not inspected.
Released 2026-09-22. Default branch also committed on 2026-10-01; repository is unarchived with recent issue activity.
Documents Linux requirements, Ubuntu and amd64 support, and upstream Meson build/test/install commands. Native macOS supervision is unsupported.
Official WSL prerequisites, Ubuntu package installation and systemd enablement. Systemd services do not keep a WSL instance alive.

layers.deciding_comparison: This is a provisional capability-fit selection, without a measured reliability winner. Compare Dagu+systemd against Prefect+systemd on WSL2 with identical persistence, retry policies and explicit process limits. Test stubborn/detached descendants, pending-retry cancellation, scheduler/worker death, WSL shutdown, restart, and crashes immediately before/after committed external effects. Measure surviving processes, duplicate/missing effects, recoverable history, recovery time, resource use and operating effort. If host-loss survival or long waits are required, qualify Temporal against Restate using the same effect/recovery cases. The packet's unequal-configuration recovery comparison named no winner. Currency does not separate candidates: all eight are unarchived, with recent releases, default-branch commits and issue activity.
evidence_gaps: No retrieved public head-to-head measurement establishes superiority for this workload; upstream CI exercises different suites and platforms.
Per-workflow systemd containment requires explicit configuration and testing. Supervising only the Dagu server does not establish independently bounded runs.
Dagu's macOS arm64 binary is available, but its native resource guard reports unsupported enforcement and continues with a warning. The selected systemd complement requires Linux.
External-effect idempotency, compensation and storage recovery remain workload-specific. Stale-state repair, retries and durable execution alone do not prove safe effects.

Prefect implements process-group termination, but universal launch-path wiring and detached-descendant coverage were not verified. Temporal and Prefect check-context samples were paginated; failure causes were not inspected.
Version correction: Dagu shutdown-signal propagation is documented in examined HEAD documentation, but was not established for v2.18.1. The pinned release's Ubuntu unit checks succeeded.
